description: Yehuda et al. measured methylation within FKBP5 in Holocaust survivors (n=32), their adult offspring (n=22) and controls (n=8 and n=9). At bin 3 / site 6, survivors showed higher methylation than controls and their offspring showed lower; parent and offspring levels correlated significantly.
energy_note: A measurable mark in a child who was not there.

aspect: Why FKBP5 rather than any other gene
description: FKBP5 regulates glucocorticoid receptor sensitivity and is independently linked to PTSD and major depression - the same HPA-axis machinery implicated in the somatic and cardiovascular consequences in PTS-003.
energy_note: The stress thermostat, and its setting.

aspect: The replication, and what it narrowed the mechanism to
description: A 2020 American Journal of Psychiatry study replicated the decrement at intron 7 site 6 in offspring, with the effect predominating in offspring of mothers exposed in childhood - implicating maternal developmental programming rather than germline inheritance.
energy_note: Through the mother's own childhood, not through sperm.

aspect: Site specificity argues it is not noise
description: Offspring methylation at bin 2 / sites 3-5 was instead associated with the offspring's own childhood abuse interacting with an FKBP5 risk allele. Different sites tracked parental versus personal trauma, which is a stronger result than a single association.
energy_note: Two different injuries, two different sites.

aspect: Supporting endocrine findings from the same cohorts
description: Maternal age at exposure and maternal PTSD independently influence urinary cortisol in adult offspring; elevated 11beta-HSD type 2 activity in offspring; NR3C1 glucocorticoid receptor methylation differs by which parent had PTSD.
energy_note: Several instruments, pointing the same way.

aspect: HONEST LIMIT - the sample was tiny and the mechanism is contested
description: 32 survivors, 22 offspring, 8 and 9 controls. Critical commentary focuses on whether this supports true germline epigenetic inheritance at all, versus in-utero exposure or postnatal transmission. The replication points at the latter two.
energy_note: Real finding. Much smaller than the headlines.

description: It does not mean a grandchild has inherited PTSD, that an outcome is fixed, or that anyone's condition is explained by an ancestor's war. It means an altered regulatory setting on a stress-response gene, associated with vulnerability, in a specific cohort.
